---
title: "Missing data"
---

Missingness is a relation among a linguistic unit, an intended measurement, and its realized record. A blank cell does not identify that relation by itself. A missing-data analysis must state the unit, the measurement that should have been available, and the process that made an observed value unavailable. We represent availability with a binary [random variable](../random-variables-and-distributions/why-random-variables.qmd): it maps each eligible unit to one when the intended value is recorded and to zero when it is unavailable.

This module develops that specification with two linguistic resources whose fields
and provenance we inspect directly. The first is the MIT-licensed Tanaka sentence
collection in [Jacy](https://github.com/delph-in/jacy/tree/82c282e2592841478d07aa81a83489344bb16e00),
whose Redwoods-style selection workflow is described by
[Tanaka et al. (2005)](https://aclanthology.org/P05-1041/) and
[Bond, Kuribayashi, and Hashimoto (2008)](https://www.anlp.jp/proceedings/annual_meeting/2008/pdf_dir/PC1-7.pdf).
Its outcome is availability of a grammar-generated, human-selected analysis. The
second is the nonimputed release of
[Hillenbrand et al.'s (1995) vowel measurements](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.411872),
distributed in a [permissioned repository](https://github.com/santiagobarreda/hillenbrand_et_al_1995/tree/6dd44decc8ef5b537cbb54732a3b00c8fa652e65).
Its missing values are unavailable F2 or F3 measurements for recorded vowel tokens.

The collection moves from observed missingness patterns and mechanism claims through complete-case deletion, then develops low-rank imputation and a separate masking design for validating it.

Here are the two row types before we count anything. Jacy item `tc-006::109000` is the sentence *彼 は その 運動 に 関係 が ある の です か 。* It has 12 whitespace-delimited profile tokens, 11 grammar readings, and one selected analysis. A Hillenbrand row such as `b01ae` is one recorded /hVd/ word, here /hæd/ from speaker `b01`; its columns record duration, F0, and steady-state F1--F3 in milliseconds or hertz. The [Jacy dossier](missingness-patterns.qmd#jacy-measurement-dossier) and [Hillenbrand dossier](complete-case-analysis.qmd#hillenbrand-measurement-dossier) define these fields and their limitations in full.

```{r}
#| label: missing-data-index
#| message: false
#| warning: false

jacy <- read.csv(
  "data/jacy-mrs/tanaka-selection.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
hill <- read.csv(
  "data/hillenbrand-raw/hillenbrand-raw-formants.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

jacy_state <- ifelse(
  jacy$preferred_analysis_count > 0L,
  "Selected Jacy analysis",
  ifelse(jacy$parse_readings > 0L, "Parsed, unselected", "No positive reading")
)
steady_columns <- c(
  "duration_ms", "f0_hz", "f1_steady_hz",
  "f2_steady_hz", "f3_steady_hz"
)

module_inventory <- data.frame(
  empirical_object = c(
    "Jacy sentence items",
    "Jacy items with a selected analysis",
    "Hillenbrand vowel tokens",
    "Tokens complete on five steady measurements"
  ),
  count = c(
    nrow(jacy),
    sum(jacy_state == "Selected Jacy analysis"),
    nrow(hill),
    sum(complete.cases(hill[steady_columns]))
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(jacy) == 15000L,
  sum(jacy_state == "Selected Jacy analysis") == 8670L,
  nrow(hill) == 1668L,
  sum(complete.cases(hill[steady_columns])) == 1617L
)

module_inventory
```

```{r}
#| label: inspect-missing-data-records

jacy[jacy$profile == "tc-006" & jacy$item_id == 109000L,
     c("profile", "item_id", "item_text", "item_length",
       "parse_readings", "preferred_analysis_count")]
hill[hill$token_id == "b01ae",
     c("token_id", "speaker_type", "speaker_id", "vowel", "ipa",
       "duration_ms", "f0_hz", "f1_steady_hz",
       "f2_steady_hz", "f3_steady_hz")]
```

The first record shows an observed endpoint of the Jacy pipeline: its analysis was selected. The second shows an acoustic token whose five steady measurements are all observed. Later pages compare these records with items whose pipeline endpoint or acoustic cell is unavailable.

These two absences have different meanings. An unselected Jacy item lacks an accepted result from a grammar-and-selection pipeline; it is not thereby a sentence without meaning. A Hillenbrand `NA` marks an unavailable acoustic estimate, not 0 Hz and not the absence of the vowel token. This distinction governs every method that follows.

## What counts as missing?

Several superficially similar absences still require different analyses.

- **An absent record:** a speaker who was never recruited or a corpus token that
  was never sampled has no row. Only a unit represented in the realized table
  can have a missing cell. Extending the analysis to unrepresented speakers or
  tokens instead requires a sampling or coverage argument.
- **Planned missingness:** a counterbalanced experiment may deliberately leave some participant--item combinations unpresented. Those omissions belong to the [design](../experimental-design/counterbalancing.qmd); they are not accidental nonresponses.
- **An undefined measure:** a word skipped on first pass has an observed skipping outcome, but no first-pass fixation duration. Reading studies consequently analyze skipping and fixation-contingent durations as distinct measures ([Rayner et al. 2011](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3543826/)). Coding the duration as `NA` does not create an unseen fixation duration.
- **Measurement or analysis failure:** the record exists, but a value that the protocol intended to recover is unavailable. The Hillenbrand formant cells belong here, though the release does not identify a cell-specific cause.
- **Dropout:** a participant begins a longitudinal or multi-session study but
  supplies no later records. The observation process has lost that participant's
  later measurement occasions as a block, so the relevant dependence and target
  concern unit-level retention over time.

These cases may all produce blanks after data are reshaped into a rectangle. But they imply different target populations, different observation processes, and different possible remedies. Imputation is relevant only after we have identified a value that was intended to be observed and is now unavailable.

## From locations to assumptions

We proceed in two steps. First, [missingness patterns](missingness-patterns.qmd) represent which intended values are observed. The indicator describes locations; it does not explain them. Second, [missingness mechanisms](missingness-mechanisms.qmd) state how the probability of observation may depend on named observed and unobserved variables. The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR are incomplete unless those variables and the unit of analysis are specified.

This distinction parallels the separation between a sampling design and an outcome model. The pattern is observed data. The mechanism is an assumption about the process that produced that pattern.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

[Complete-case analysis](complete-case-analysis.qmd) retains rows observed on every variable required by a particular analysis. It thus defines a selection indicator. If selection depends on the response or a predictor, the retained rows may describe a different population from the eligible rows.

[Iterative PCA imputation](pca-imputation.qmd) takes a different route. [Principal component analysis](../factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd) finds orthogonal directions that successively account for variance in a centered measurement matrix; a [rank-$K$ reconstruction](../factorization/reconstruction.qmd) retains only the first $K$ directions. Iterative imputation uses that reconstruction to update missing cells while returning observed cells to their measured values. The resulting number is a model-based prediction under a low-rank assumption. The recording itself remains unavailable, and a single completed matrix does not propagate uncertainty about the prediction.

Finally, [validation by artificial masking](validating-imputation.qmd) hides some observed values, fits the full procedure without them, and compares the held-out reconstructions with their known values. This extends the earlier distinction between [training and test data](../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.qmd) to matrix cells. It can reveal reconstruction failures under the tested masks, but it cannot reveal the values that were naturally missing.

The order of the module follows the decisions an analysis requires: (i) specify what
should have been observed, (ii) describe where it is absent, (iii) state assumptions
about why, (iv) make deletion explicit, (v) define one reconstruction method, and
(vi) test that method under artificial masks fixed before we compare ranks. A blank
becomes statistically interpretable only after we name its unit, variable, and
observation process.

## Check the specification

1. What does Jacy selection record, and what additional evidence would be needed to infer grammaticality? **Answer:** selection records the endpoint of a particular grammar-and-annotation pipeline. A grammaticality claim would require a separate judgment measure or a validated link between this pipeline and Japanese speakers' judgments.
2. How do a missing formant marker and the numeric value 0 encode different claims? **Answer:** `NA` records an unavailable estimate, whereas 0 would assert that an acoustic measurement equals 0 Hz.
3. When is imputation even a candidate remedy? **Answer:** only after the intended unit and measurement exist and the realized value is unavailable. It does not create units that were never sampled or quantities that the protocol leaves undefined.

## Recap and route through the module

1. Missingness relates a unit, an intended measurement, and an observation process.
2. The Jacy and Hillenbrand tables instantiate different units and different meanings of absence.
3. The next page begins with the [Jacy measurement dossier](missingness-patterns.qmd#jacy-measurement-dossier), then constructs the observed missingness pattern that later mechanism and remedy pages must explain.
